headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of grid infrastructure costs, aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Data Center Costs.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger amended HB 1393 to ensure residential customers are not subsidizing data center costs, restricting Dominion Energy's spending and capping its return on equity. These amendments aim to save money for residential customers by shifting more energy-related expenses onto large industrial users.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities supplying data centers to report their water consumption to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency on resource usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Data Center Water Usage Reporting Requirements Advance.
news_summary: SB 553, along with a similar House bill, passed the legislature, requiring water utilities to report data center water consumption. This legislation aims to provide clarity on water usage and allow for impact consideration during rezoning decisions.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to require comprehensive site assessments, including noise studies and environmental impact reviews, for new data center developments.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, environmental groups, neighborhood associations, Del. Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, commercial real estate associations.
news_headline: Virginia Data Center Siting Restrictions Gain Traction.
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on noise, agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval. This legislation provides localities with more tools to evaluate and regulate data center impacts on surrounding communities.
